result.title: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: Mitigating Rubric Hacking through Latent Dimension Recovery and Balancing
result.summary: Rubric hacking limits both performance and training robustness in rubric-based reinforcement learning. By decomposing rubrics into sub-dimensions, we reveal the Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: as the total rubric score increases, certain sub-dimension scores systematically decrease, suggesting the model sacrifices specific quality aspects to optimize the aggregated objective. From the sub-dimension perspective, we observe two phenomena: (1) dimension imbalance, causing the policy to favor heavily covered dimensions; (2) dimension absence, leading to a systematic gap between rewards and true quality. To mitigate these issues, we propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA), which has generations compete within each dimension separately to mitigate rubric imbalance, and Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC), which mines evaluation dimensions implicitly encoded in a holistic preference signal to complete rubric coverage. Experiments in chat, science, and medical domains indicate that FRDA mitigates rubric hacking with more stable improvements, while RSDC outperforms both single-reward training and naive multi-reward aggregation, yielding generally higher-quality responses.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 rubric 强化学习中的「rubric hacking」：将评分标准分解为子维度后，发现总分上升时部分子维度得分系统性下降，并据此提出 FRDA（子维度内竞争以缓解维度失衡）与 RSDC（从整体偏好信号中挖掘隐含评价维度以补全覆盖）两种方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其子维度分解、从整体信号中恢复隐含维度的做法，可能为 latent 推理训练中的奖励设计与贡献分配/监督提供可核查线索，但论文面向纯文本 RLHF，未涉及视觉推理状态。
